item.title: Staff Post - Wikiwalk Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Timer expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. - Hide Block

Alright. So this one is mostly self-contained. However, the mention of the MTF in the final addenda could be altered so that instead of a one-shot MTF it would be MTF Iota-10 under the guise of DEA agents. This is both in character for this particular MTF and matches with the narrative of the rest of the addenda. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

Mobile Task Force 73 is investigating a report that a drug cartel located in ██████████, Mexico, is kidnapping members of the public, breeding SCP-456, and extracting the narcotics produced by the victims. Anyone found to be using SCP-456 in this manner is to be terminated.

To this:

Mobile Task Force Iota-10 ("Damn Feds") is investigating a report that a drug cartel located in ██████████, Mexico, is kidnapping members of the public, breeding SCP-456, and extracting the narcotics produced by the victims under the cover of DEA operatives. Anyone found to be using SCP-456 in this manner is to be terminated.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
Like a few others, I've had the unfortunate experience of having to deal with a bed bug infestation. It is not fun. It makes me want to go on an insect genocide.

It was everything I could do to not downvote solely because of my hatred for these wretched little bastards, but then I realized that the near-universal hatred of these things is precisely why bed bugs are an SCP.

Good work. But personally, this is one of those things I'd make an exception to the "Contain and protect" philosophy.

What would be the point of continuing experiment 456-4? Also, this doesn't even sound anomalous to me. No vote.

item.title: Re: Addendum
item.content:encoded:
Precisely. Nature has come up with things far worse than this. Some of the parasitoid wasps are pure nightmare fuel, controlling the behavior of their prey in ways that'd be sci-fi/horror material in humans.

Along that line, I'm highly ambivalent about this one. It gives me the appropriate "AUGH getitoff ohgod" vibe, but it's nothing that couldn't actually evolve. Numerous parasites already inject anaesthetics, such that their hosts don't notice their presence; numerous others kill their hosts, some with absurd speed. (Ebola, anyone?) This is unlikely but nowhere near impossible.

No vote from me for now.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
They need to be something that needs to be kept secret from the public, and something that the Foundation would benefit from studying. This isn't the strangest insect, and the public will be surprised by it, but nothing more. If it did need to be secret, the Foundation would simply destroy it. They have no reason to keep it alive, even considering how little resources it would use.

Also, it should be significantly more creepy than insects in the wild. That said, this has proven nearly impossible. We still make insect SCPs because they're still creepier than most SCPs.

item.title: Addendum
item.content:encoded:
I don't think the comment about terminating people cultivating this SCP belongs here. The Foundation doesn't care about drug dealers… If anything, I would suspect the directive to have field agents either infiltrate such groups in order to locate possible sources of the bug, or simply firebomb the cultivation sites (read: the VICTIMS, not the cartel members) to remove more 456 from the wild.

Also, euphoria AND sleepiness? At the same time? Because that's how this sounds to me… Yeah, I'm nitpicking :-)

Otherwise, not bad at all!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
they dont need to be supernatural, but this isnt quite even into the realm of the "abnormal". it doesnt exist, but this would be a legitimate evolutionary strategy i could see a species of insect developing.

classifying them as an SCP doesnt make much sense, there's nothing about them that needs to be "contained" inherently. this would be like classifying any dangerous species as an SCP. if the public was aware of these they'd have to be cautious in case they had them, but it'd just mean pesticides.

i like the idea of this one and your writing on the article is good. it's scary in concept, and the idea of it possibly being real does make it just that much worse. but i do think it needs something more to push it into SCP territory. not voting yet.

http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-611 an example of an insect species that in and of itself isnt necessarily so much more dangerous, and it could be called a legitimate evolutionary strategy, but reaches into the realm of….how to say it….that which if the public knew about they would be scared crapless. you're not off base here or anything, i just think this needs a little more than it currently has
